rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 is the best design so far (score 711.2). The oval finished 20/20 (progress 0.997). The s-bend finished 18/20 (progress 0.977, 2 off-track exits). The slalom never finished: 0/20 runs, progress 0.77, 1.05 line-loss events per run, steering_oscillation 0.45 and control_effort 14.3, the highest of any track. Slalom is therefore the bottleneck, and the failures are overshoot and line loss rather than a lack of sensing. Compared with iteration 4 (same gains, sensors at y=0.05), moving the array to y=0.065 and widening it to ±0.042 raised slalom progress from 0.31 to 0.77, so the sensing change helped. The jitter also rose with the change (oval oscillation 0.18 to 0.30, slalom 0.23 to 0.45), which points to the loop being too aggressive for the bends now that it sees the line earlier.

Changes: (1) base_speed lowered from 1.1 to 0.95, so the robot has more time to correct on the slalom's quick direction changes and each line loss has less overshoot. The finish-time term is worth at most 60 points and changes by only a few points for this speed change, while a completed run is worth 500. (2) kd lowered from 0.5 to 0.45. The oscillation grew after kd moved from 0.4 to 0.5, so this trims derivative amplification of the signal jitter. kp stays at 3.0, since that gain is what gave the progress and the oval result. (3) Geometry is kept identical to iteration 5, so this race isolates the speed and damping effect.

Expected result: slalom line_loss_events near 0.5 or below, steering_oscillation near 0.3 or lower, and slalom progress above 0.9. A first slalom finish is plausible. The oval should still finish, with a completion time of about 2.2 s. Hypotheses: (a) lower speed reduces the overshoot that drives slalom line loss; (b) a small kd reduction cuts jitter without removing the damping needed for the bends. Failure signs: if slalom progress stays near 0.77 with the same line losses, the limit is the steering authority, so the next step should be a modest kp increase or a wider array. If oscillation rises above 0.4, kd is still too high relative to the sensor lead. Next measurements: progress and line_loss_events on slalom and s-bend, steering_oscillation and max_error on all tracks, and completion_time on the oval to check the speed margin.
